clusters.name: doc
clusters.executionModeRationale: A standalone markdown design doc with no code overlap; runs fully in parallel with everything else.

clusters.name: wire
clusters.executionModeRationale: Isolated new wire schema in a separate package; no overlap with happy-cli/happy-server work, so it runs in parallel with doc.

clusters.name: spawn-initmsg
clusters.executionModeRationale: Pre-existing-bug fix (add initialMessage to SpawnSessionOptions + thread through spawnSessionFromSession) with no async-events/router dependency; lands in phase 1. scope-bc serializes after it because US-007 also edits the spawn path.

clusters.name: core
clusters.executionModeRationale: New router module that imports the wire schema; serialized after wire for the type dependency, otherwise isolated.

clusters.name: scope-bc
clusters.externalPrereq: async-events-design: packages/happy-cli/src/agentComms/mailbox.ts + daemon POST /agent-comms/send must be on origin/main before this cluster's async-events-dependent work (US-004, US-005b Scope C message fixture, cross-session delivery in US-007) starts. The US-005a initialMessage-propagation fix is split into the independent spawn-initmsg cluster and lands earlier.
clusters.executionModeRationale: These stories co-edit the stdio bridge and control server (local message + spawn tools), so they MUST serialize within one cluster to avoid conflicting edits; also gated on the async-events mailbox landing (see externalPrereq).

clusters.name: scope-a
clusters.executionModeRationale: Touches disjoint files (Dev Tunnels manager, happy-server ingest route + config slot, CLI shim, peer modules) from scope-bc, so it runs in parallel with scope-bc in phase 3; start after core's router public types are stable (it imports the envelope + resolver), not merely after file creation.
